The captioned appeal is by the claimants questioning the quantum of compensation determined by the Tribunal in MVC Sumangalamma And Ors vs Basanagouda And Anr on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170180616/
2 No.127/2019.

entities.text: MVC Sumangalamma And Ors vs Basanagouda And Anr on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent - insurance company has admitted its liability.
2. The appellants/claimants, who are widow, two children and mother of the deceased have filed a claim petition for having lost one Bhattappa in a road traffic accident dated 31.01.2019.
Though appellants claimed that deceased was earning Rs.4 lakhs per annum, the Tribunal in the absence of income proof assessed the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.11,000/-.

Though there is no income proof, this Court is of the view that income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.11,000/-
notionally is on the lower side.

In the absence of income proof, placing reliance on the income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, income is assessed at Rs.13,250/- per month and by adding 40%, NC: 2024:KHC-K:8238 income is assessed at Rs.18,550/-.

Since there are four dependents, 1/4th is deducted and income is assessed at Rs.13,912/- and by applying a multiplier of 15, compensation under the head of loss of dependency works out to Rs.25,04,160/-.
3. Under the conventional heads Rs.1,90,000/- is awarded.

By extending the benefit of escalation at the rate of 10% for every three years in the light of principles laid down by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi1, an additional sum of Rs.19,000/- is paid on the conventional head at Rs.1,90,000/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.27,13,160/- as against Rs.15,55,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

4. In the light of the discussion made supra, following order is passed:
(2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC-K:8238 ORDER a) Appeal is allowed in part.

b) Appellants/claimants are entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.11,58,160/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till its realization.

c) The apportionment shall be made as per the order of the Tribunal Sd/-
(SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM) JUDGE SRT CT-SW Sumangalamma And Ors vs Basanagouda And Anr on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170180616/
